74cb8653a1971d3707c6bfd8614db10c3e5711f6.summary: A 2015 blog post by MobileIron (Michael T. Raggo, October 2015) on XARA, a group of iOS and OS X vulnerabilities reported by Indiana University researchers. It describes URL scheme hijacking, where a malicious app registers the same URL scheme as a legitimate app, intercepts inter-app requests, and can be used for phishing and credential theft. The researchers say their discoveries date back to fall 2014, and FireEye's Masque Attack II (February 2015) is cited as earlier work. Mitigations are MobileIron's AppConnect product and general iOS best practices.

74f9ea2e6d18b6e38364e1645f4b0d2620d01245.summary: Quorum Cyber profiles Scattered Spider (also known as UNC3944 and Roasted 0ktapus), a financially motivated group reported active since at least May 2022. The report says it gains initial access mainly through stolen credentials from SMS and email phishing, and has used Azure Serial to reach administrative console access on virtual machines. It is also reported to use a STONESTOP loader to install a signed driver, POORTRY, which terminates security software in a bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver attack. The group is said to phish other users from the employee database and move laterally.
